surfaces.part: windshield and rear glass (sloped blue glass)
body side with doors and wheels

answer.evidence: The car body has flat top surfaces seen from above: the roof (rows 5-16, ending in a dark edge line at row 17 above the side windows) and the hood and trunk (rows 13-24, with highlights, ending in a light edge line at row 25). Below them the south side face runs from about row 25 to 41, with doors, a body-side panel and wheels. This gives a top surface of 12 rows plus a front face of 17 rows, so it reads as three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The car body is a dark grey ramp of about 3-4 steps plus a bluish window tone. It is outlined by a uniform near-black/neutral line around the whole silhouette; 89% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 0-1% for the tinted hedge and cheese-stall outlines. That is the 'sticker' look the standard rejects, since Beodeul outlines use the dark tone of the adjacent material. The large body panels, roof and doors are smooth, nearly flat fills with only a thin highlight line. Texture is limited to window glints and wheel details, with no grain or speckle. At 8 visible tones per tile it falls well short of the stall (17) and well (20), and is roughly level with the hedge (9). Overall the car is clean and readable but flatter and more sticker-like than the references, so it fails.

answer.evidence: The hood and trunk are wide gray bands (rows 13-24, with a highlight) that end in a lighter front-edge line at row 25. The body side with the doors, handles and lights runs below it to about row 41. The roof is a flat panel (rows 5-16) closed by a dark edge line at rows 16-17, and the slanted glass planes beside it read as a top-view surface. The wheels and door side form a front face of about 17 rows, so the body has both a top surface and a front face. The car is oriented left. No receding isometric side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The car body is a dark grey with a lighter top edge and a few window highlights, so only about 3 lightness steps on the body ramp against 5-6 on the references. The outline is a uniform near-black/dark-grey line around the whole silhouette (89% of dark edge pixels are near-neutral), which is the 'sticker' look. The references use tinted dark-material edges: hedge 0% neutral, stall 1%, well 33%. The body panels, roof and lower sides are large, smooth areas of one grey. The measured 14% near-flat coverage is similar to the cheese stall (13%), but the hedge and well sit at 0%. With 8 visible tones per tile against 9 for the hedge and 17-20 for the stall and well, the candidate is at the low end. The wheels, windows and bumpers are clearly readable, but the body has no grain, speckle or reflection dots. A neutral grey car is a legitimate theme choice, but the structure is shallow: a neutral outline, a flat body and few shading steps.

surfaces.part: windshield and rear glass (sloped glass planes)

answer.evidence: The car is a left-facing body whose south side shows doors, a beltline and wheels, rows 26-41. Above it the hood and trunk decks (rows 13-24) end in a light beltline edge at row 25 with a darker row just above, which is evidence (a). The roof panel (rows 6-16, tapering from width 26 to 44) ends in a dark edge at row 17 and is also a top surface. The sloped windshield and rear glass add further top-plane evidence (c). The body has both a top surface and a front face of more than 3 rows, so it reads as three-quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The car is a neutral grey/black body with a dark outline running all around it. 89% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline is a uniform near-black line, the 'sticker' look, rather than a tinted dark tone of the adjacent material. Beodeul references such as the hedge (0% neutral), the cheese stall (1%) and the well (33%) use tinted outlines. The body panels show about 3-4 grey steps (highlight, mid, dark, deep) and the windows have a simple light/dark split. That is shallower than the 5-6 steps on the references. The body, roof and door areas are broad smooth fills with only a few highlight lines and no grain, speckle or per-part variation, and 14% near-flat coverage is above the hedge and well at 0%. It has 8 visible tones per tile against 9 for the hedge, 17 for the stall and 20 for the well, so it sits at the low end of the references and well below the richest ones. The shape reads clearly as a car, and the wheels and lights are tidy. But the neutral outline, shallow ramps and flat panels would look thinner and more sticker-like next to the stall and well.

answer.evidence: The car is drawn from the side, but the hood and trunk decks (rows 13-24) and the roof panel (rows 5-16) read as horizontal planes with a gloss streak. Row 25 is a light belt line, a front-edge line that closes the hood and trunk decks. The roof's own edge line is the dark row 17 above the glass. Below that, the door and side body form a front face of about 16 rows (26-41), with wheels at rows 33-45. The top surfaces are foreshortened and only loosely separated from the side view, so this is a borderline reading.

styleAnswer.evidence: The car body is a dark grey with one or two lighter shades, a blue-grey window, and a uniform near-black outline around the whole silhouette. 89% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 0-1% for the hedge and cheese stall, which use tinted outlines. That is the sticker look. The body panels, roof and doors are large flat areas with little grain or speckle (14% near-flat coverage, comparable to the cheese stall's 13%, but the car's flat areas are the main body surfaces). It has 8 visible tones per tile against 17-20 for the stall and well, and about 9 for the hedge. The wheels and window have little internal shading or highlight clusters, so the shading is shallow at about 3 steps per material against 5-6 in the references. Compared with the stall and well, it looks thinner, flatter and more outlined.
